# Spec: item-kinds
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-10-02 -->

## Overview

Board item HEF-10 (report 18 #6; the deck's slides 32–33: the vulnerability and incident workflows are
the feature pipeline with a different source board and **one extra check before monitoring**). Every
board item is dispatched the same way today. This feature gives an item a **kind** — `feature`
(default), `incident` or `vulnerability` — read mechanically from a marker on its heading (🐞 incident,
🛡 vulnerability; configurable), recorded on the ledger entry, and turned into one extra, **required**
verifier gate: an incident fix must come with a regression test that cites the item id and passes; a
vulnerability fix must leave `/hef.scan` (and `/hef.scan --deps` when a manifest changed) clean of the
finding the item names. The implement worker is told the kind too, so it writes the regression test
first. A verify run that omits the kind's gate is treated as a failure — the gate is not a suggestion.

Decisions taken here rather than left as clarifications: the kind lives in `item_kind` on the entry
(`kind` already names the board source); detection is `status-board.sh --item-kind <id>`, which scans
the heading tokens before the id for any marker in the kinds map (so a state marker written by
`ledger publish` in front does not hide it); the map is `kinds` in the project config over the default
`{"🐞":"incident","🛡":"vulnerability","🛡️":"vulnerability"}`; the two new verdict gates are added to
the ledger's `GATES`; the required-gate rule is enforced by the launcher's transcription, not by the
prompt alone.

## User Scenarios

### US1: The heading decides the kind [P1]
- **Given** `## 🐞 HEF-21 — login fails after token refresh` in TODO.md
- **When** `/hef.orchestrate` registers it
- **Then** `status-board.sh --item-kind HEF-21` prints `incident` and `ledger.sh init … --item-kind
  incident` records `item_kind: "incident"`
- **Edge**: `## ⏸ 🛡 HEF-22 — …` (a publish state marker first) → `vulnerability`; no kind marker →
  `feature`; a config `kinds` entry `{"🔥":"incident"}` is honoured
- **Error**: no such item → non-zero, as `--item` does; `--item-kind` with an unknown value on `init` →
  non-zero naming the three kinds

### US2: The worker knows what kind of fix it is making [P1]
- **Given** an `incident` entry
- **When** `session-launch.sh implement` builds the prompt
- **Then** the prompt adds: write a failing regression test that cites `<id>` first, then the fix, and
  the test must pass; a `vulnerability` entry's prompt adds: name the finding, fix it, re-run
  `/hef.scan` (and `--deps` when a manifest changed) before the PR
- **Edge**: `feature` → no addition (the prompt is byte-identical to today's)
- **Error**: none — the kind is data the launcher already validated at `init`

### US3: The kind's gate is required, not suggested [P1]
- **Given** an `incident` entry verified by a session that returns only `review` and `quality` verdicts
- **When** the launcher transcribes the verify result
- **Then** it records the two verdicts, then a synthesized `incident FAIL` verdict with evidence "gate
  missing from the verifier's report", and blocks on `verdict`
- **Edge**: the verifier returns `incident PASS` with evidence → the normal path (pr, human:merge)
- **Error**: `incident FAIL` → blocked on `verdict` as any FAIL

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `status-board.sh --item-kind <id>` (tasks-repo; refused for github-project like `--item`; id validated like `--item`; searches todo, doing, backlog like `--item`): prints `incident`, `vulnerability` or `feature` from the first heading carrying the id — any whitespace-separated token before the id that is a key of the kinds map (config `kinds` over the default `{"🐞":"incident","🛡":"vulnerability","🛡️":"vulnerability"}`); no such item → non-zero | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `ledger.sh init … [--item-kind feature\|incident\|vulnerability]` records `item_kind` (absent flag → `feature`); any other value — **including an empty one**, the signature of a failed detection swallowed by `$(…)` — → non-zero naming the three; `ledger.sh record <id> --item-kind <k>` sets it on an existing entry (an item that gains 🐞 after registration); `GATES` gains `incident` and `vulnerability` | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | `/hef.orchestrate` step 1 registers each item as `KIND=$(status-board.sh --item-kind <id>) && ledger.sh init … --item-kind "$KIND"` (the detection's exit code is never swallowed); the brief names a non-feature kind | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | `session-launch.sh implement`: for `incident`, the prompt adds the regression-test-first rule citing `<id>`; for `vulnerability`, the name-fix-rescan rule; for `feature`, nothing | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | `session-launch.sh verify`: for `incident`/`vulnerability` the chain gains the kind's gate (incident: "a test in the diff cites `<id>` and passes — show the test name and the runner output"; vulnerability: "`/hef.scan` (and `/hef.scan --deps` if a manifest changed) is clean of the finding the item names — show the output"), the schema's gate enum includes both kinds, and the transcription synthesizes `<kind> FAIL` when the kind's gate has no PASS/FAIL verdict — absent (evidence "gate missing from the verifier's report") **or SKIPPED** (evidence = the verifier's reason) — before deciding pass/block; only the entry's OWN kind gate is added to the chain and the schema enum | P1 | US3 |
| FR-006 | Docs: `docs/hooks.md` (`--item-kind`, `item_kind`, the gates), `docs/install.md` §7 (heading markers), README §5 one line, `CHANGELOG.md`; board HEF-10 → DOING | P2 | US1 |
